text: The $(c-2,c)$ split. Pair at weight $c-2$ and put the second factor in the centre: if $x_i^{E_i}\in\gamma_{c-2}$ and $g_i\in(\gamma_c)^{2^{c-4}E_i}$, then $X_i(g_i-1)\in\Delta^{2c-2}$ (as Lemma 8: $2^{c-4}E_iX_i\in\Delta^{c-2}$), with the multiplier 2 at class 5, as in (3.12). (Lemma 7 then holds only modulo $\Delta^{2c-4}$; the error terms are larger.) [on paper, sketch] In a Lie ring this cannot carry $D_{2c-2}$: the retraction of the proof of [IMP26, Theorem C] (onto $T$, vanishing on $Z(T)\cdot T$) kills $\sum_i(e_ix_i)\zeta_i$ with $\zeta_i$ central, while it fixes $a$; in the shifted family the $\gamma_c$-part of $g_i$ comes only from binomials ($E_ld_l=-\binom{E_l}2[d_l,x_l]$), so it is zero in the ring. text: What is proved is about the method, not the groups: for a presentation of the shape (3.12) (paired generators with $x_i^{E_i}\in\gamma_{c-1}$, $w=\prod[x_i,x_j^{A_{ij}}]$), $w-1$ splits as in Lemma 7; $w\ne1$ forces a pair with $A_{ij}<E_iE_j$ (Lemma 9); for that pair the pairing lemma certifies the binomial error only up to $\Delta^{c+1}$ (Lemma 10) and the pairing part only up to $\Delta^{k+\min(2+\log_2 m,k)}$. So any proof of $w\in D_8$ at class 5 in this family must get two levels from relators other than the power relators of the paired generators, plus the multiplier 4 (or a cancellation between $S$ and the errors). In every group measured, the levels gained were exactly the carriers' count (Table in (c)). A theorem $f_{\rm met}(5)=7$ would need an upper bound for $D_8$ that does not go through this decomposition; nothing here gives it.

text: So c5i5 fails at $D_8$ exactly as c4a fails at $D_7$ and L2g at $D_7$: in the pairing part $S$ (multiplier 2 where 4 is needed, (b)) and in the binomial error of the $w$-pair, through the same monomial $2E_2X_2^2X_1$. The carrier $x_5$ does not lift the binomial error from the certified $\Delta^{c+1}=\Delta^6$ to $\Delta^8$: at most one level, as at class 4 (the parts were not measured at $n=7$; there only $w\in D_7$ is known, §6.10). This is what conjecture H predicts; the alternative "$S$ only" (H false) is excluded. H stays a conjecture (two groups, one per class).

text: [on paper, every step checked by computer] The identity is short. Move the scalar $128=2E_2=16E_1$ from $X_2$ onto $X_1$: $$128X_2^2X_1\equiv X_2^2\,(x_1^{128}-1),\qquad x_1^{128}=P_1^{16}=d_2^{-16}d_3^{-64}=x_5^{1024}\,d_3^{-64}\pmod{\Delta^6},$$ then $X_2^2(x_5^{1024}-1)\equiv1024X_2^2X_5\in\Delta^6$, because $512X_2^2\in\Delta^5$ (Lemma 13, a "quadratic pairing"), and $64X_2^2D_3=(64X_2)X_2D_3\in\Delta^{2+1+3}$. Only the relators of $x_1$, $x_2$, $x_5$ and class $\le4$ are used (Theorem 14). Without the carrier the same steps end in $-16X_2^2D_2$, which is $\notin\Delta^6$ [computer].
section: 6.12. D5-10: the carrier identity, why it buys one level, and what a class-5 design needs

text: [on paper] So the carrier turns the $d_2$-part $d_2^{-16}$ of $x_1^{128}$ — a small power of an element of $\gamma_k$, which $X_2^2$ certifies only to $\Delta^5$ — into a large power $x_5^{1024}$ of a generator, which the quadratic pairing absorbs. The $d_3$-part $d_3^{-64}$ is not carried: plain pairing puts it in $\Delta^{k+3}$, which is $\Delta^6$ at class 4.
section: 6.12. D5-10: the carrier identity, why it buys one level, and what a class-5 design needs

text: [on paper] Lemma 15: once the pairing holds with multiplier 1, $w=[x_2,x_1^{A_{12}}]=\prod_l[x_2,d_l]^{-a_lA_{12}/E_1}$ ($P_1=\prod_ld_l^{-a_l}$), and every $d_l$-part that pairing alone can certify contributes $1$. So $w\ne1$ needs a part that pairing cannot certify, i.e. a carried part: the carrier is forced, not incidental.

The prediction "at $n=7$ the piece $64X_2^2D_3$ fails and the carrier piece and the binomials of $x_1$ do not" is confirmed [computer, Modal A10G, certified]: the identity holds modulo $\Delta^7$ with only $64X_2^2D_3\notin\Delta^7$ (see (b)).

text: (c) [on paper] Conditions for $NX_2^2X_1\in\Delta^{2k}$ ($N=A_{12}/2$): each $d_l$-part of $x_1^N$ is either carried by a power $x_\kappa^F$ of a generator with $2^kE_2\mid F$, or has $v_2(a_lN/E_1)\ge e_2+k-3$ (Proposition 16, sufficient); a second carrier is called for when two parts fail the second condition. For c5i5 the $d_3$-part fails ($64<2E_2$), which is why $128X_2^2X_1\notin\Delta^8$ there (§6.11(g)). [computer] Seven presentations built: the second carrier on c5i5 (c5i6, six generators), two multiplier-4 designs and four one-change variants — $w=1$ in $M=\Gamma/\gamma_6\Gamma''$ in every one ((d)). The only group of this family with $w\ne1$ at class 5 is still c5i5.

With the test record of §6.11 (c4a = $G$ of plateau5_c4i5, 1 554 relators: the 9 of (3.12), 45 metabelian, 250 of $\ker\varphi$, 1 250 commutators of weight 5), dropping the 5 relators $d_l^{N_l}$ and the two top ones, or the 45 metabelian ones, or the 250 of $\ker\varphi$, keeps $128X_2^2X_1\in\Delta^6$ (certified); dropping the relator of $x_3$ keeps it too (membership found, the certificate needs other $h$ and was not redone); dropping the relator of $x_1$ or of $x_2$ loses it (not certified for the same reason), and so does dropping that of $x_5$ (§6.11, certified). Moving the scalar around: in c4a, c4b and c4a without $x_5$'s relator ($h=(2,1,2,0)$, $r_6=47$, certificate holds), with $e_1=2D_1X_2X_1$, $e_2=32D_3X_2X_1$, $e_3=32D_5X_2X_1$, $e_4=32X_2^4X_1$: $128X_2^2X_1\equiv e_1+e_2-e_3+3969\,e_4$ (the relator of $x_2$), $e_2,e_3,e_4\in\Delta^6$ in all three, and $e_1\in\Delta^6$ only in c4a: the whole effect sits in $2D_1X_2X_1$, which is again $128X_2^2X_1$ read through the relator of $x_2$. text: Lemma 13 [on paper] (quadratic pairing). Let $k\in\{3,4\}$, $G$ of class $\le k+1$, $x^E=P=\prod_ld_l^{e_l}$ with $d_l\in\gamma_k$, $E=2^e\ge4$, $X=x-1$, $s\in\{0,1\}$, $2+s\le k$. Suppose that for every $l$ either $E\mid8e_l$, or $d_l^{2^{s+3}e_l}\in\gamma_{k+1+s}$. Then $2^{s+3}E\,X^2\in\Delta^{k+2+s}$.
section: 6.12. D5-10: the carrier identity, why it buys one level, and what a class-5 design needs

text: Proof. $x^E-1=\sum_{m\ge1}\binom EmX^m$, so $2^{s+3}EX^2=2^{s+3}(P-1)X-\sum_{m\ge2}2^{s+3}\binom EmX^{m+1}$. Modulo $\Delta^{2k}$, $P-1\equiv\sum_le_lD_l$. A term $2^{s+3}e_lD_lX$ is $D_l\cdot\frac{8e_l}E\,(2^sEX)\in\Delta^{k+2+s}$ in the first case (pairing lemma of §6.7: $2^sEX\in\Delta^{2+s}$), and $(d_l^{2^{s+3}e_l}-1)X\in\Delta^{k+2+s}$ up to $\Delta^{2k}$ in the second. For $m=2$: $2^{s+2}E(E-1)X^3$ is $(4EX)X^2\in\Delta^{\min(4,k)+2}=\Delta^{k+2}$ for $s=0$ and $(E-1)X(8EX^2)\in\Delta^{k+3}$ for $s=1$ (by $s=0$). For $m\ge3$, $v_2\binom Em=e-v_2(m)$, so the term is a unit times $(2^{s+3-v_2(m)}EX)X^m$, of level $\ge\min(2+\max(0,s+3-v_2(m)),k)+m\ge k+2+s$. $\square$
